newsitem.title: SWEDEN: TENNIS-FRENCH IN DAVIS CUP DRIVING SEAT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-FRENCH IN DAVIS CUP DRIVING SEAT.

text.p: France took command of the Davis Cup final on Saturday when Guy Forget and Guillaume Raoux upset the fancied Swedes in the doubles for a 2-1 lead with two matches to play.

With Stefan Edberg injured and doubtful for Sunday when he was to play the fifth match of the tie, France, who started as clear underdogs, now have a fine chance to capture the trophy for the second time this decade.

Edberg, who twisted his ankle during his straight-sets defeat by Cedric Pioline on Friday, watched from courtside as team mates Jonas Bjorkman and Nicklas Kulti went down 6-3 1-6 6-3 6-3 to the fired-up French pair.
The match swung dramatically with each player succumbing to the tension in the huge echoing converted boat-builders shed staging the tie.
But it was Bjorkman, recently returned to action after a knee injury, who proved the most fragile, dropping his serve four times and making frequent unforced errors.

He lost his serve in the fourth game of the first set to allow the French pair first blood. He and Kulti, who have won two doubless titles together this year, then took advantage of a temporary loss of French nerve to capture the second set in just 22 minutes.

But, after a brief pep talk from captain Yannick Noah, the French roared back to take the next five games in a row, Raoux's power complementing Forget's deft touch. The Swedes won three games from 5-0 down but could not stop the French taking the lead again.
Bjorkman suffered once more in the fourth set, dropping serve in the sixth game and in the last when Forget whipped in a forehand winner to clinch the victory.
Forget, a member of the 1991 Davis Cup winning side, used all the experience of 12 years of Olympic and Davis Cup tennis, punishing anything wild, volleying precisely and producing some fine passes.
"Guy Forget played excellently. They deserved to win," a subdued Swedish captain Carl-Axel Hageskog said afterwards.
Hageskog has the headache of deciding whether to risk Edberg on Sunday or play one of the losing doubles pair.
He told reporters he would make no decision until just before the matches, which pit Thomas Enqvist against Pioline and Arnaud Boetsch against Edberg or his substitute.
Enqvist earned Sweden their only point so far when he beat Boetsch on Friday.
Edberg trained gently on Saturday after the doubles match, jogging carefully round the court five times and then hitting across the net for 20 minutes.
Earlier x-rays had shown he had slightly damaged a tendon in his right foot, with swelling and bleeding in the soft tissue.
"There's going to be a question mark over him until right before the match," Noah said, adding he doubted the veteran Swede, who retires after the tie, would play.
"We are prepared for anything to happen. But it is better to be in our situation than the Swedes," he added.
